title: The Commander Boomer Shooter - Full Roster Bible

portability.logic: pure Rust - damage math, AI state machines, encounter scripting, audio scheduling, taunt selection, pickup rules, weapon stats
portability.engine: UE5/Blender-side - meshes, skeletons, materials, textures, lighting rigs, level geometry, particles
portability.contract: This file is the ONLY interface between the two. The Rust runtime reads these numbers verbatim; no value here is re-derived in code.

roster.name: Sectoid
roster.silhouette: small + gaunt, oversized smooth cranium, symmetric glowing eyes, NO mouth
roster.signature: luminous eyes, no mouth, bare skull - reads as a praying thing with nothing under the hood

budget.deck_note: one emissive channel (eyes), no GI dependency - reads on emissive alone

roster.name: Viper
roster.role: ranged line unit, plasma rifle pressure
roster.silhouette: tall + narrow reptilian hunter, forward-projecting elongated snout, raised ribbed dorsal spine, plasma pistol held out front
roster.signature: 45 cm forward-projecting snout, five-rib dorsal spine, plasma pistol with a glowing coil

budget.deck_note: plasma coil emissive is the second light source in the silhouette

roster.name: Floater
roster.role: hovering psi attacker, ignores ground cover
roster.silhouette: LEGLESS broad manta parasite: ONE continuous swept planform tip to tip, low segmented glowing dorsal core, NOTHING under the body
roster.signature: 2.5 m span, no legs at all, a body-shaped hover ellipse is the only thing beneath it

budget.deck_note: cheapest asset in the kit - no legs means no leg animation cost; hover ellipse is a decal, not geometry

roster.name: Muton
roster.role: armoured line breaker, heavy plasma rifle, area denial
roster.silhouette: heavy + wide armoured slab, horizontal emissive visor slit, huge pauldrons, two-handed plasma rifle, oxblood chest plate
roster.signature: the only creature in the kit with a horizontal visor slit; the oxblood chest plate is the focal point

budget.deck_note: oxblood accent is the ONLY warm hue in the alien set - keep it to one material instance

roster.name: Chryssalid
roster.role: fast flanker, leaper, closes distance hard
roster.silhouette: low + wide forward-pitched stalker on four long digitigrade legs, two scythe forelimbs sweeping forward, venom glow
roster.signature: a fast crouch - readable in pure silhouette at 40 px tall

budget.deck_note: 4 legs + 2 scythes = the highest bone count per tri; keep animation on 2 bones at a time

roster.name: Barnacle Drone
roster.role: cheap swarm unit, zone denial near water
roster.status: DESIGNED (blockout E_BarnacleDrone.uasset exists; v2 mesh not built)
roster.silhouette: clustered shell cone on three stubby legs, single red eye-lens
roster.signature: wet shell-clicking idle; red eye-lens pulses 0.6 s before the spit

budget.deck_note: 3 spawns per wave - LOD0 only, 512px textures

roster.name: Pilgrim Zealot
roster.role: musket rifleman, holds lanes, shouts FOR THE KING on attack
roster.status: DESIGNED (blockout E_PilgrimZealot.uasset exists; v2 mesh not built)
roster.silhouette: hunched pilgrim in a ruffed collar, long musket held across the body
roster.signature: the red ruffs explode outward when it dies

budget.deck_note: cloth is the only material - no cloth sim, baked to the mesh

roster.name: Mayflower Phantom
roster.role: long-range glass sniper, low aggression, punishes standing still
roster.status: DESIGNED (blockout E_MayflowerPhantom.uasset exists; v2 mesh not built)
roster.silhouette: translucent tattered sail-cloak, hollow hood, no visible feet
roster.signature: materialises out of fog on a glass-shatter precursor

budget.deck_note: translucency is a dithered mask, not a blend - cheapest honest ghost on Deck

roster.name: Lobster Brute
roster.role: pit gatekeeper, very high aggression, closes to melee
roster.status: DESIGNED (blockout E_LobsterBrute.uasset exists; v2 mesh not built)
roster.silhouette: armoured lobster torso, two huge asymmetric claws, sub-bass rumble idle
roster.signature: claws charge with static and snap audibly 1.0 s before the hit

budget.deck_note: hard shell = high roughness, cheap specular - no clearcoat

roster.name: Rock Golem
roster.role: platform gate, slam AoE, high HP, low speed
roster.status: DESIGNED (blockout E_RockGolem.uasset exists; v2 mesh not built)
roster.silhouette: blocky granite mass, no neck, glowing orange cracks in the shoulders
roster.signature: cracks glow orange 1.5 s before the slam, 0.8 s recovery window after

budget.deck_note: 16 bones - the least animation cost of any heavy

roster.name: Nor-Easter Titan
roster.role: storm boss, phase-2 shield regen, projectile storm
roster.status: DESIGNED (blockout E_NorEasterTitan.uasset exists; v2 mesh not built)

phases.note: standard - Mayflower Cannon is the answer
shield regenerates if not hit; rocket splash clears projectiles

roster.silhouette: storm-front mass, cloud skirt, lightning-forked arms
roster.signature: sky darkens and lightning strikes BEFORE the charge - 1.8 s of free warning

budget.deck_note: the only 2048px asset in the game; at 'low' it drops to 1024 with a 4th-mip bias

roster.name: Tobias Angell
roster.role: resistance contact inside the settlement; opens a route, or trades a marked hostile for shells
roster.status: DESIGNED (no blockout asset; v2 mesh not built)
roster.silhouette: lean upright dockworker, stovepipe cap and belted oilskin, hand lantern held low, face unreadable at 40 px
roster.signature: he trades in marks: a hostile he has seen is worth 30 rounds of Light ammo to him

budget.deck_note: one cloth material baked to the mesh - no cloth sim, ever

roster.name: Edda Cobb
roster.role: yard rigger; restores a piece of hardware, which opens a route and lights the yard
roster.status: DESIGNED (no blockout asset; v2 mesh not built)
roster.silhouette: broad upright rigger in bib overalls and a canvas coat, one oversized spanner carried like a bat
roster.signature: she repairs under fire and complains about it; the floodlights come up as a side effect

budget.deck_note: tool and coat share one material - the spanner is the only separate part

roster.name: Dr. Wren Hollis
roster.role: harbour wireless operator and former medical orderly; stabilises the player, reads out the boss's weakness
roster.status: DESIGNED (no blockout asset; v2 mesh not built)
roster.silhouette: slight upright figure in a long cardigan, headphones round the neck, a notebook never put down
roster.signature: she reads the boss out loud while it is happening, which is the only reason the player knows its weakness

budget.deck_note: notebook and headphones are one material - no separate props pass

roster.name: Cyberdisc
roster.role: hovering shield projector; the only enemy that makes the player shoot something they cannot damage
roster.status: DESIGNED (no blockout asset; v2 mesh not built)
roster.silhouette: flat disc hovering with no limbs, raised emitter ring on the rear third, three radial vents, no organic curvature anywhere
roster.signature: unmistakably a machine: hard concentric rings and one amber emitter lens, and it never once pretends to be alive

budget.deck_note: 14 bones and one emissive - the cheapest field projector on the Deck

roster.name: Bionic Chryssalid
roster.role: heavy cybernetic variant of the Chryssalid; the only enemy that deletes the player's cover
roster.status: DESIGNED (no blockout asset; v2 mesh not built)
roster.silhouette: the forward-pitched Chryssalid stalker rebuilt on hydraulic legs, plate instead of chitin, walking where the organic one leaps
roster.signature: it shears whatever cover is within 700 uu, so the fight moves instead of the shooting

budget.deck_note: 32 bones is the highest count in the kit - animate 3 at a time or it stutters

roster.name: the Oysterman
roster.role: human-appearing infiltrator walking the settlement in oilskin; kills at contact once it is close
roster.status: DESIGNED (no blockout asset; v2 mesh not built)
roster.silhouette: a man in a belted oilskin and sou'wester, carrying an oyster crate in both hands, walking like every other man in the street
roster.signature: TELL: the cast shadow has a bare head - the sou'wester's brim is missing from the shadow, so the shadow and the body disagree

budget.deck_note: the shadow is a decal on a proxy mesh - one extra draw, no shadow-casting light needed

roster.name: the Lampwright
roster.role: variant of the Oysterman in a canvas coat with an unlit storm lantern; the shadow is correct, so the other tell is the only tell
roster.status: DESIGNED (no blockout asset; v2 mesh not built)
roster.silhouette: a woman in a long canvas coat with an unlit storm lantern held out from the hip, unhurried, deliberate, wrong
roster.signature: TELL: the lantern glass shows a different, younger face, and the reflection does not move with her

budget.deck_note: one extra vfx system for the glass reflection - it is a second render of the head, not a mirror

roster.name: the Ice Man
roster.role: heaviest variant, ice delivery on a shoulder yoke; the slowest of the three and the hardest to see coming
roster.status: DESIGNED (no blockout asset; v2 mesh not built)
roster.silhouette: a broad delivery man with an ice block on a shoulder yoke, wide and slow, a load wider than his shoulders
roster.signature: TELL: his boot prints sink four times deeper than his weight accounts for, and there is no drag mark behind the yoke

budget.deck_note: yoke and ice are one material - the load never chips, so the silhouette stays clean

bosses.name: The Harvester
bosses.concept: Pac-Man's grid-eat pursuit and Sonic's momentum, fused into one X-COM organism. It moves on a lattice, eats the arena's power nodes to grow, and when it stops eating it ROLLS.

budget.deck_note: 7 materials is the cap - merge the two dark chitin materials before ship

attacks.name: pellet-eat
attacks.notes: the boss eats a power node; the node heals it and is the denial target the whole fight is built on

attacks.name: roll
attacks.notes: the roll along the arena rail; it cannot turn, so the exposed back is the vulnerability

attacks.name: famine-lunge
attacks.notes: straight-line charge across the grid; damage cut from 55 to 45 so the global telegraph rule stays honest

attacks.name: glowing-pepperoni-pizza
attacks.flight: burped out of the maw on a 45 degree lob, decelerating under 600 uu/s2, spinning about its axis, apex at 1.5 s, then it lands and bursts
attacks.counter: shoot it out of the air - the pizza has 20 HP and two Puckle rounds kill it, in which case no cheese pool ever forms; if it is not shot, dash clear of the landing ring, which is lit on the floor for the full 1.2 s tell
attacks.notes: the only Harvester attack the cheap gun can answer, which is how the fight teaches the player that the Puckle matters

attacks.name: shriek
attacks.notes: the 1926 foghorn, the one that killed nine men - phase 3 entry

taunt_rotation.selection: pure Rust: phase-gated, no immediate repeat, 1.5 s minimum gap, 6.0 s maximum gap
taunt_rotation.channel: the taunt channel ducks the music bed by 6 dB and never ducks weapon SFX

budget.deck_note: see roster entry plymouth_titan

acts.name: I - THE BATTERY
acts.beat: Player enters from the south, crosses the arena, climbs the pillar to the green keycard, drops into the pit for the red one
acts.turn: The player learns the fog lies: the way *out* is through the thing that looks like a wall

acts.name: II - THE YARD
acts.beat: The crane yard: a maze of stacked containers, the loading gantry overhead, the aliens working
acts.turn: The player learns the aliens are **workers**, and the boss is **management**

acts.name: III - THE ROLL
acts.beat: The **Harvester** arrives - a boss that eats the arena
acts.turn: The player learns it is not here to conquer; it is here to **collect**, and the level is a shipping manifest

silhouette_rules.rule: a flat disc on nothing, with a raised emitter ring on the rear third - reads as a hovering disc, never as a bird, an insect or a UFO
the Chryssalid you already know, but standing on hydraulic legs - it does not leap, it walks, and it reads as heavy

machine_readable.reads_as: the fast stalker, wrong-weight and machine-jointed

silhouette_rules.rule: a man in oilskin with an oyster crate, and the sou'wester's brim is missing from his shadow

tell.observable: the cast shadow has a bare head - the brim is absent from the shadow, not from the body
tell.learned_at: act 1 scripted near-miss at the fish store, then taught outright by Tobias Angell
tell.difficulty: readable at 20 m under a street lamp; useless in flat fog

silhouette_rules.rule: a woman in a canvas coat with an unlit storm lantern, and the lantern glass shows a face that is not hers

tell.instrument: lantern glass, window panes, wet hull plating
tell.observable: the reflection in the glass is a different, younger face, and it lags her movement
tell.learned_at: her first appearance in act 2; her shadow is deliberately correct, so the Oysterman's tell does not fire on her
tell.difficulty: needs a reflective surface - the level guarantees one within 40 m of every Lampwright

silhouette_rules.rule: a delivery man with an ice block on a shoulder yoke, and his boot prints sink like a loaded cart

machine_readable.reads_as: an ice delivery man, loaded and slow

tell.observable: the prints are four times deeper than his weight accounts for, and there is no drag mark behind the yoke
tell.learned_at: seen on the beach road, then again in the yard
tell.difficulty: needs soft ground - the level guarantees a patch of wet sand within 30 m of every Ice Man

friendly_support.opens_route: sea-wall service lane (act 1 to act 2 connector)
friendly_support.route_effect: the bolted service door at the fish store swings open; the lane skips the whole battery approach

intel_trade.gives: one hostile marked on the map for 25 s

presence.fallback: the door is found unbolted after 45 s of searching - same route, no intel, 45 s lost
presence.death_penalty: the door stays bolted for the act; the player can force it with 3 Sextant Scattergun blasts (3 Heavy rounds)

friendly_support.restores: the shore crane hoist and the yard floodlights
friendly_support.route_effect: the hoist raises the container bridge - a second route into the yard
friendly_support.visibility_effect: the floodlights kill the fog concealment skin jobs depend on, so their shadows and reflections become legible

presence.fallback: the hoist stays dead for the act; the player climbs the container stack by hand in 12 s, fully exposed, with no floodlight and no second route

friendly_support.stabilises: one field dose per act, restoring 40 HP as a one-time pickup - the no-regen rule is unchanged
friendly_support.reads_out: the Harvester's hunger is its weakness: the open mouth is a x2 damage window, and the power node can be baited
friendly_support.readout_window: act 2 gantry, then once per boss phase over the wireless

presence.fallback: no readout; the player has to take the x2 mouth hit once in the first 30 s of the fight to learn it

cutscene_beats.name: The battery watch
cutscene_beats.camera: locked low behind the 12-inch breech on a 35 mm lens, fog at knee height; the frame does not move until the telephone rings, then a slow 1/3-stop push to the handset on the parapet

shots.camera: locked low behind the gun breech, 35 mm, muzzle out of frame right
shots.action: the battery ticks, a gull, nothing else
shots.line: VOICE ON PHONE (distant, wet): Commander? You are still on the line. Good. Good good good.

shots.camera: slow push toward the field telephone on the parapet, 50 mm
shots.action: the telephone rings - a wet clicking, not a bell
shots.line: MERCY DUNNE (radio): Don't shoot yet. They have not looked up.

shots.camera: pan left to the fog line, 50 mm, a pier lamp guttering
shots.action: the fog thins; the pier is full of things and they are working
shots.line: VOICE ON PHONE: You are on the manifest. Number one.

shots.camera: 85 mm, shallow focus, the handset on the deck
shots.action: the clicking stops
shots.line: VOICE ON PHONE: Your shift starts now.

cutscene_beats.name: The contact at the slipway
cutscene_beats.trigger: player enters the slipway trigger volume
cutscene_beats.camera: no camera takeover - first person at 90 degrees, the contact framed in the player's own light, the view allowed to drift 10 degrees so he never sits dead centre; gameplay never pauses

shots.camera: first person, 90 degrees, angell lit from below by his own lantern
shots.action: he does not stop working while he talks
shots.line: TOBIAS ANGELL: You are the battery. I have been waiting for the battery.

shots.camera: first person, 10 degree drift left, the fish store door in frame
shots.action: he nods at the bolted service door
shots.line: TOBIAS ANGELL: That door opens the sea wall. Twenty minutes on the sand, or four if you are clever.

shots.camera: first person, hold on the lantern, the fog behind him
shots.action: he counts shells into his hand
shots.line: TOBIAS ANGELL: Thirty rounds and I will mark one of them for you.

shots.camera: first person, widen to include the pier fog
shots.action: he looks at the pier and stops talking for a moment
shots.line: TOBIAS ANGELL: I may not be here when you come back. I have not been here for eight days.

cutscene_beats.name: The green keycard
cutscene_beats.camera: a crane that rises with the player up the pillar on a 24 mm lens, sodium lamp blooming as it climbs, then a 1.5 s hold on the settlement below with the fog behind it

shots.camera: 24 mm, camera rising with the player, pillar rungs in the near field
shots.action: the climb, the sodium lamp swinging in frame
shots.line: VOICE ON PHONE: Climb. Look at it from above and it stops pretending.

shots.camera: 24 mm, craning past the player, the town opening out below
shots.action: the green keycard glow pulses once on the parapet
shots.line: MERCY DUNNE (radio): Green card is yours. The red one is in the pit. Do not go in the pit.

shots.camera: 28 mm, hold on the settlement, fog wall moving in behind it
shots.action: the hold - the town, and the wall of fog eating it from the seaward side

cutscene_beats.name: The loading gantry
cutscene_beats.camera: a 24 mm dolly along the loading gantry, container stacks passing close to the lens, work lights only; the camera never stops moving, because the yard is a production line and the shot is a conveyor

shots.camera: 24 mm, dolly starts on the gantry rail, container corner filling the left third
shots.action: an alien passes below carrying a crate like a porter
shots.line: TOBIAS ANGELL: They are not invading. They are loading.

shots.camera: 24 mm, dolly continues, gantry leg crosses frame right to left
shots.action: a second and third alien move a crate between them, working
shots.line: TOBIAS ANGELL: Every box out of that yard has a label. Everything out of that yard is a shipment.

shots.camera: 35 mm, dolly slows, the camera cranes down through the stacks
shots.action: the yard opens out: rows of crates, all of them labelled
shots.line: MERCY DUNNE (radio): Ours. All of those are ours. I labelled the first one myself, in 1919.

shots.camera: 50 mm, push on one crate's shipping label
shots.action: the label reads PLYMOUTH, MASS, and a number

cutscene_beats.name: The hoist repair
cutscene_beats.trigger: player reaches the shore crane winch
cutscene_beats.camera: no camera takeover - first person, the repair is read on the winch itself rather than on the HUD, and the camera holds still so the player can cover the approach while they work

shots.camera: first person, the winch drum filling the frame
shots.action: she drops the spanner into the drum teeth and starts
shots.line: EDDA COBB: Hold this lever or hold the gun. Not both, love.

shots.camera: first person, slight dip as the player crouches to the housing
shots.action: the hold-repair progress reads on the winch drum
shots.line: EDDA COBB: Eleven seconds. I have counted them. I was a signal corps clerk, I count everything.

shots.camera: first person, the yard lights coming up as the hoist turns over
shots.action: the floodlights strike and the fog thins - every shadow in the yard appears at once
shots.line: EDDA COBB: There. Now you can see the shadows. Look at the shadows.

shots.camera: first person, hold on the container bridge as it lifts
shots.action: the second route opens
shots.line: EDDA COBB: Bridge is up. And I will not be here tomorrow, so take the light with you.

cutscene_beats.name: The manifest
cutscene_beats.camera: 85 mm macro on a paper manifest under a lantern, the camera drifting slowly across the column of names until it reaches the Commander's line; the paper is the scariest object in the game and the shot says so

shots.camera: 85 mm macro, lantern light raking across the paper, no wider than the page
shots.action: a column of names in a clerk's hand

shots.camera: 85 mm, slow lateral drift down the column
shots.action: the names are dates as well as names - 1919, 1921, 1924
shots.line: MERCY DUNNE (radio): It has been collecting since before I wrote that first label.

shots.camera: 85 mm, drift stops on one line
shots.action: the line reads PLYMOUTH, MASS - and the Commander's name, with a weight beside it
shots.line: VOICE ON PHONE: Ah. There you are. I have been holding your crate.

shots.camera: 85 mm, the paper lifts slightly in a draught that should not exist
shots.action: the hold, the page, the name

cutscene_beats.name: The Harvester arrives
cutscene_beats.trigger: first crossing of the harbour rail
cutscene_beats.camera: a low 21 mm push from the harbour water as the Harvester crosses the rail, its six legs unfolding one at a time; the camera never rises above the dorsal hump, so it never reads as a face; the last frame is the boss's own shadow sweeping across the lens

shots.camera: 21 mm, low over black water, the rail seam glowing ahead
shots.action: the seam lights up - the roll is coming
shots.line: DR. WREN HOLLIS (wireless): It is on the rail. Do not stand on the rail.

shots.camera: 21 mm, slow push as the legs unfold, the body rising out of the water
shots.action: the maw opens once, tasting the air
shots.line: VOICE ON PHONE: I have the whole yard in my mouth. I only need the rest of you.

shots.camera: 21 mm, hold, the boss filling frame, the camera still below the dorsal hump
shots.action: it eats a crane leg - the geometry stops existing
shots.line: DR. WREN HOLLIS (wireless): It is eating the level. That is the boss. The rest is scenery.

shots.camera: 21 mm, the boss's shadow crosses the lens, blacking out the frame
shots.action: the frame goes to black on the shadow
shots.line: VOICE ON PHONE: Do you like pizza? I ask because I am about to be very badly made at you.

cutscene_beats.name: The readout
cutscene_beats.camera: no camera takeover - the readout arrives as a subtitle and a single HUD prompt while the fight continues; the game never pauses a boss fight to explain itself

shots.camera: gameplay camera, no change, the fight continues in full view
shots.action: the boss is mid-bite, mouth open
shots.line: DR. WREN HOLLIS (wireless): It chews. It has to. That is the whole of it - it has to eat.

shots.camera: gameplay camera, unchanged
shots.action: the HUD prompt fades in over the open mouth
shots.line: DR. WREN HOLLIS (wireless): When it opens, it is not looking. Put everything in the mouth.

shots.camera: gameplay camera, unchanged, the player takes the shot
shots.action: the player shoots the open mouth
shots.line: DR. WREN HOLLIS (wireless): Twice the damage. I read it off the manifest. It cannot digest a full crate.

cutscene_beats.name: The first roll
cutscene_beats.trigger: arena cleared of stragglers, before the boss engagement
cutscene_beats.camera: 35 mm at rail height so the player sees the seam light pass across the floor, locked off while the body goes over, then a cut to the HUD fading in as control returns

shots.camera: 35 mm, camera on the floor at rail height, the seam glowing
shots.action: the seam lights, 0.8 s before the roll
shots.line: DR. WREN HOLLIS (wireless): The seam. It lights before it comes. It is the only warning you get.

shots.camera: 35 mm, locked off, the body passes over the lens
shots.action: the roll, fast, over the camera in a second
shots.line: VOICE ON PHONE: Faster. Faster. I am being late on a manifest.

shots.camera: 35 mm, the boss at the far end of the rail, back turned
shots.action: the exposed back - the first thing the player is shown to shoot
shots.line: DR. WREN HOLLIS (wireless): Its back. When it rolls it cannot turn. Put the cannon in the back.

shots.camera: 35 mm, the HUD fading up over the shot
shots.action: control returns

tts_contract.word_count_rule: every rendered line is 15 words or fewer and carries exactly one thought

render_cost_measured.note: measured on the HTPC F5-TTS service; the service ignores a speed parameter, so line length is the only cost lever

tts_contract.cost_model: a bank of long lines renders in hours instead of minutes - the 40-line bank is roughly 2.8 hours at 251 s per line against about 38 minutes at 57 s
tts_contract.bank_working_limit: the bank's own validator is stricter than the contract: taunt_lines.py enforces MAX_WORDS = 10 and MIN_WORDS = 5, measured at ~1.38 s of speech per word
tts_contract.selection: phase-gated, no immediate repeat, 1.5 s minimum gap, 6.0 s maximum gap
tts_contract.priority: the taunt channel ducks the music bed by 6 dB and never ducks weapon SFX
